title: Mouth sores: what you can do yourself
intro: Mouth sores such as canker sores and cold sores are very common and usually heal within a week or two without treatment. They can be painful, but simple measures reduce discomfort and speed healing. Persistent or unusual sores should be examined to rule out other causes.

sections.heading: Types of mouth sores
paragraphs: Canker sores, or aphthous ulcers, are small, round, painful ulcers inside the mouth with a white or yellow centre and red border, and are not contagious. Cold sores are blisters on or near the lips caused by herpes simplex virus and are contagious. Other causes include injury, ill-fitting dentures, burns from hot food, infections like thrush, certain medicines and some illnesses.

sections.heading: Triggers
paragraphs: Canker sores can be triggered by small injuries, stress, hormonal changes, some foods such as acidic or spicy items, deficiencies of iron, vitamin B12 or folate, and certain conditions like coeliac disease. They often recur in some people.

sections.heading: Self-care
paragraphs: Avoid spicy, salty, acidic and very hot foods and rough foods such as crisps. Rinse gently with salt water, or use soothing mouth gels or rinses available at pharmacies. Use a soft toothbrush and avoid toothpastes with sodium lauryl sulfate if they irritate. Painkillers like paracetamol or ibuprofen can ease pain. Cold sores may respond to antiviral cream when used early, and the virus can spread through close contact, so avoid kissing and sharing items.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor
paragraphs: Seek advice if a sore lasts more than two to three weeks, grows, bleeds, is accompanied by lumps in the neck, fever or difficulty swallowing, or if you have frequent sores. Smoking and heavy alcohol use raise the risk of mouth cancer, and non-healing sores should be assessed promptly. Large or frequent sores may need prescription treatment or investigation.

sections.heading: Prevention
paragraphs: Maintain good oral hygiene, treat dentures that rub, manage stress, eat a balanced diet and note foods that trigger sores. Use sunscreen on lips to help prevent cold sores triggered by sun.

examples.title: Soothing a canker sore
examples.text: Imagine you have a painful ulcer inside your cheek. You could avoid acidic foods, use a gentle rinse and a pain-relief gel, and expect improvement in about a week.

examples.title: Noting a lasting sore
examples.text: Suppose a sore on the side of your tongue has not healed after three weeks. You might arrange a dentist or doctor visit rather than waiting longer.
